content: All Children’s Hospital, located in St. Petersburg, Florida, is a dedicated pediatric hospital and the only freestanding children’s hospital on the Gulf Coast of the state. It is recognized as a leader in pediatric care, education, research, and advocacy. The hospital has consistently been ranked among the top 25 children’s hospitals in the United States by Child Magazine, which named it the best children’s hospital in Florida in 2007. Additionally, All Children’s Hospital has received accolades such as the Most Outstanding Business awards from the Tampa Bay Business Journal and the Greater St. Petersburg Chamber of Commerce. This private, not-for-profit institution traces its origins to Florida’s first Crippled Children’s Hospital, which was established to care for children affected by polio. The hospital’s mission extends beyond treating diseases; it emphasizes the importance of teaching and research to advance cures for pediatric illnesses. All Children’s Hospital collaborates with the University of South Florida (USF Health) and the H. Lee Moffitt Cancer Center & Research Institute to share its expertise in pediatric medicine through research and education. As a regional referral center, the hospital provides care for children with some of the most complex medical conditions, drawing patients not only from across Florida but also from all 50 states and 36 foreign countries. Due to increasing regional demand, construction is underway for a new hospital and outpatient center to replace the current 40-year-old facility. This $300-million project, expected to be completed in 2009, will encompass nearly one million square feet of space dedicated to state-of-the-art pediatric healthcare. On September 1, 2007, Karoline and Ben Byler of Wesley Chapel welcomed sextuplets—five boys and one girl—delivered at All Children’s Hospital. The babies, weighing between 2 and 3 pounds each, were born prematurely and required intensive medical care. Among them, Ryan Patrick was in critical condition, while Jackson Robert’s condition was upgraded from critical to serious. Charlie Craig and MacKenzie Margaret were listed in serious condition, and Brady Christopher and Eli Benjamin were in stable condition. As of now, all but one of the babies are reported to be in fair condition. The Bylers had conceived the sextuplets with the assistance of fertility drugs.
